prompt: Is there an idea in Buddhism of a four way truth in which something can be true, false, both true and false, and neither?
judge_reasoning: The correct idea in Buddhism is the tetralemma/catuṣkoṭi (a four-cornered way of treating a proposition as true, false, both, or neither). Candidate 1 directly answers the prompt but incorrectly denies that this framework exists. Candidates 2 and 4 discuss Buddhist theories of truth (emptiness, dependent origination, etc.) but never provide the requested four-way true/false/both/neither structure. Candidate 3 focuses on the Four Noble Truths, which is unrelated to the “four-way truth” logical form asked about.
